clue.text: Drink in second working men's club?

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a crew is a team of working men
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink at a working men's club for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: A working men's club is a British social club with a bar; here the phrase is split into crew and a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice.

clue.text: Glass sailing ship

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall glass for sherry or beer
second meaning: a fore-and-aft rigged vessel with two or more masts

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a glass-bottomed boat, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a large drinking vessel for sherry or beer and a type of rigged vessel.

clue.text: Managed on extremely grotesque cooking stove

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremities of a word, its first and final letters only

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
first and last letters of grotesque

explanation.surface: Someone coped with a hideous old kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with ovens and hotplates.

clue.text: Tedious beginning to weeks one's had in each European capital

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something had in another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: first letter of weeks
EA is the usual abbreviation for each
the Italian capital city
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: A dull account of weeks spent touring each capital city of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' could be any city; the letters of 'one's' must fit inside it, which points to the Italian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiring through dullness, a synonym of tedious.

clue.text: Instructions on how to cook piece of rump, oddly-shaped piece

indicators.note: only a small part, the opening letter, of the following word is used
something oddly shaped has its parts bent out of their usual form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of rump
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Cooking directions for a cut of rump steak in an odd shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is the set of directions for preparing a dish.

clue.text: Lotion used by The Invisible Man?

definitions.text: Lotion used by The Invisible Man?

blocks.note: surface reading: a skin cream of some kind
setter's reading: H. G. Wells's hero disappears, so his cream would make one disappear

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the literal sense of the name of a light, quickly absorbed face cream: a cream that makes you disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a real cosmetic, a light moisturiser that soaks into the skin without trace.

clue.text: Consideration shown by some Hampshire spectators

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, a run of their letters

blocks.note: runs across the end of the county name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Fans watching a match in Hampshire are treated thoughtfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Respect means regard or esteem, a sense of consideration for others.

clue.text: Oppose drunken sister

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to an inebriated sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or withstand, a synonym of oppose.

clue.text: Reels on a poster ingeniously advertising a cassette player

indicators.note: something done ingeniously is cleverly reworked, so the letters are cleverly rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever poster showing tape reels promotes a portable tape machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal stereo, like the Walkman, is a portable player for cassette tapes heard through headphones.

clue.text: Satirical novel now here for editing

indicators.note: text given for editing is due to be reworked, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical manuscript has just arrived to be edited.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's title is itself almost 'nowhere' backwards, which makes the choice of fodder apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Erewhon is Samuel Butler's 1872 satire set in an imaginary country.

clue.text: Stresses account is in need of a small amount of money

indicators.note: a thing in need of something must take it in to be complete, so the last piece goes inside

blocks.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account
is shortened to 's
a cent is a coin worth a hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: A worried note that an account is short of a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' shrinks to the apostrophe-s ending, as in 'account's', and the coin sits before that ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Accents are the emphases placed on syllables, so stresses in speech.

clue.text: Approaching trendy retail outlet

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Someone nearing a fashionable shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase: what is in store is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store is coming soon, so the phrase means imminent or approaching.

clue.text: Deadlock — one at front of maisonette's out of date

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: Roman numeral for one
first letter of maisonette
passé means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A stand-off over a maisonette whose front looks dated.
explanation.walkthrough: A maisonette is a British flat on two floors of a larger building.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a stalemate.

clue.text: Offer to pay novice

blocks.note: to tender is to offer formally
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A proposal to pay a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or beginner, originally an inexperienced settler or scout.

clue.text: What goes on in a nightclub is bewildering — in what way?

definitions.text: What goes on in a nightclub

blocks.note: to floor someone is to baffle them, so floors means is bewildering
how asks in what way

explanation.surface: A puzzled clubgoer asks how the nightclub works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bewildering' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a verb meaning floors.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor show is the cabaret entertainment staged at a nightclub.

clue.text: Raise line provided by trawlerman, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
if means provided that
first letter of trawlerman

explanation.surface: A fisherman hauls up a line he supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it up.

clue.text: Doctor, eastern, goes into cleaners' houses

indicators.note: something that goes into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: chars are cleaning women
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A doctor from the East visits the homes of cleaning staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are rooms or apartments, especially lawyers' offices, so houses or lodgings.

clue.text: Unfriendly Conservative, advanced in years

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
elderly

explanation.surface: A grumpy elderly Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is distant and lacking warmth, the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Remarkably typical in Derby, say

blocks.note: first meaning: an outstanding example of its kind
second meaning: one of the five major English flat horse races

explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the town or a hat; it is the Epsom Derby, one of England's five Classic horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an exemplary instance of a type and also names one of the big flat races for three-year-olds.

clue.text: Capital clubs given to crack US golfer

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to crack a safe or bottle is to open it
Walter Hagen, American major champion of the 1910s and 1920s

explanation.surface: A city's golf equipment handed to an American star player.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the Danish capital city.

clue.text: Hold in Lancashire town

blocks.note: first meaning: a wrestling grip applied from behind the neck
second meaning: a mill town near Burnley

explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is a county in north-west England; the town shares its name with the wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wrestling headlock and also a Lancashire town.

clue.text: Matches goddess with ultimate of gods

indicators.note: ultimate means the very last, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth
last letter of gods

explanation.surface: A goddess is equal to the greatest of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks like a verb meaning equals; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestas are short wax matches, named after the hearth goddess.

clue.text: Worker to carry in an aardvark

blocks.note: the worker ant is the usual crossword worker
to bear a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: A labourer is told to carry an aardvark indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry in' looks like a phrase; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antbear is another name for the aardvark, an African mammal that eats ants and termites.

clue.text: Not all have a high opinion of a learner driver, 19 perhaps

indicators.note: not all of a word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to admire is to think highly of
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: People are lukewarm about a new driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is NELSON, Horatio Nelson the naval commander, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was a British naval officer of the highest rank, an example of a fleet commander.

clue.text: Love affair starts to annoy my old unmarried relative

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A romance begins to irritate a spinster aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is the French word for love, used in English for a romantic, often secret, liaison.

clue.text: Withdraw cash

blocks.note: first meaning: pull out of a race or contest
second meaning: slang for money

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a trip to the cash machine; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch a horse is to withdraw it from a race, and the same word is slang for money.

clue.text: Herb used in cooking duck with sour orange

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, resembling O
the fruit's name taken as written; sour and with only dress the surface

explanation.surface: A herb goes into a dish of duck with bitter orange.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck à l'orange traditionally uses sour Seville oranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean herb related to marjoram.

clue.text: Have an argument with son cracking puzzles

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: word puzzles in a grid
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent quarrels with a son over solving puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for fighting or disputing with someone.
